5.text: Google rolled out its Gemini 4 Argon AI model across apps and Search, launched a $180 Fitbit Edge and AI app-creation tools, and announced Unity Spark with Unity. A securities fraud class action was also filed against Alphabet.

14.text: Google signed a 20-year deal with Constellation Energy to add 890 MW of nuclear capacity, part of a 3.59 GW, $4.3 billion agreement. AEP also plans a $4 billion, 702 MW Bloom Energy fuel cell project in Wyoming for Google, operational by 2028.

11.text: Berkshire built a $37.4 billion Alphabet stake, now its third-largest holding, and Greg Abel continues adding to it. Other articles cover Abel's portfolio reshaping, buybacks, and a Bending Spoons acquisition.

6.text: Alphabet’s Q2 cloud revenue rose 82% year over year to $24.8 billion, with a $514 billion cloud backlog, and the stock is up 46% over the past year. Several articles predict gains around its Oct. 28 Q3 earnings report, citing cloud growth and heavy capex.

7.text: Alphabet faces negative free cash flow from AI data center spending, with capital constraints now the sector's biggest bottleneck. Analysts warn AI capex is draining cash and debt-funded buildouts risk a bubble, though hyperscalers remain financially resilient.

15.text: Google Health made a strategic investment in Flo Health under a multi-year women's health partnership; Google's Chrome paid XBOW a $250,000 bug-bounty reward; and Lovelace launched on Google Cloud Marketplace. Speechmatics' Oak model beat Google's speech AI on medical term recall, and ex-Google executive Prashant Kancherla became SafeSpace Global's COO.

16.text: SpaceX stock rose on analyst buy ratings, a $30 billion Google GPU contract paying $920 million monthly, and launch progress, but faced skepticism over its spectrum deal and a drop below $170. Alphabet appears only as the counterparty paying SpaceX for GPU access.

17.text: Marvell’s stock has more than tripled this year amid AI-driven custom silicon and optical interconnect growth, with analysts raising targets and citing a “monster” deal, $20B FY28 and $80B FY31 revenue goals. Alphabet is not mentioned; the articles bear on it only as broad AI capex demand from big tech.

4.text: Microsoft’s AI infrastructure spending is backed by $678 billion in commercial obligations, with Azure revenue over $100 billion. Michael Burry has raised bearish bets against AI stocks, warning of a crash amid monetization concerns; Alphabet is not directly mentioned.
